title: Arc 1/5: add a deprecated-alias capability to the profile type system
summary: Net-new alias resolution, inert until a type is actually renamed.
description: Seed an alias map at profile.ts's single compile-loop site (751-752) so both byte-identical resolvers -- schema.ts:250 canonicalType and profile.ts:1032 canonicalProfileType -- pick it up for free. No type is renamed in this task; it ships inert and testable on its own.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An alias declared in a profile resolves to its canonical type through BOTH canonicalType and canonicalProfileType
profileTypeDeclaresField returns the canonical type's fields when given an alias, so lore link accepts an aliased document
An alias that collides with a declared type name or slug is rejected at profile compile time with a clear error
Mutation-tested: removing the alias lookup from ONE resolver reddens a predicted subset of cases, not all of them
npm run check exits 0 and lore check exits 0

plan: 1. Add `aliases` to TYPE_TABLE_KEYS and ParsedType; parse it in parseTypes.

2. Validate collisions: an alias must not collide with any type name or alias (case-insensitively), nor share a lower-kebab SLUG with any type or alias - slug is file identity, the same reason the existing seenSlugs check exists.
3. Add aliases to CompiledType; seed byLowerName AND bySlug for each alias in the compile loop, so both mirror resolvers pick them up unchanged.
4. Emit one schema file per alias in emitSchemaFiles - this gives drift OWNERSHIP for free, because schemaDriftFindings defines owned as whatever the emitter produces.
5. Tests: resolution through both resolvers, profileTypeDeclaresField via alias, collision rejection (name and slug), alias schema emitted and NOT reported orphaned by lore check.
6. Mutation-test: remove the alias lookup from ONE resolver and confirm a predicted SUBSET reddens, not all.
implementationNotes:
RULING RECEIVED: option (c), ALIAS OWNS ITS SLUG, removal version 1.0.0 (opum-agent; routed to opum-doc for the decision record -- cite that record once it exists, not the message).

Supersedes my own resolve-only-name proposal. The sequence matters more than the verdict. I argued resolve-only-and-prune from the modeline being a documented non-guarantee (ADR-0011 section 2). opum-agent identified that as conflating TWO SURFACES -- the modeline and the schema FILE PATH -- and pointed out that my own e2e finding (docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh referencing .lore/schemas/story.schema.json BY PATH in three loops) is the strongest available evidence that schema paths ARE consumed by path, plausibly outside this repo too. Correct, and conceded: I produced the fact and drew the narrower conclusion from it.

I then MEASURED their literal proposal instead of reasoning about it. Arc-only profile, story.schema.json retained beside arc.schema.json, lore check:
  error .lore/schemas/story.schema.json [schema-drift]: no type in the active profile owns this schema -- run `lore schema export` to prune it
  1 file, 1 error, 0 warnings
ERROR TIER. So "emit arc and leave story in place" turns lore check RED in every consuming repository, with an error instructing the user to delete the file we deliberately kept. That killed option (b) and produced option (c).

REASON OF RECORD is asymmetric risk, adopted by the orchestrator as the reason and not merely the conclusion: bounded cost of two schema files for a window, against the unbounded cost of a consumer's CI breaking silently on upgrade with no window and no signal. The contract question -- whether ".lore/schemas/ is lore-owned and regenerable" reaches a builtin LORE removed rather than a type THE USER removed -- is genuinely ambiguous and was deliberately NOT resolved. Under (c) the ambiguity stops mattering, which is the best argument for (c).

DESIGN CONSEQUENCE THAT MAKES THIS CHEAP: schemaDriftFindings defines "owned" as whatever the generator emits, because it compares committed bytes against emitSchemaFiles output. So emitting the alias path from emitSchemaFiles yields BOTH the file and its drift ownership in one change -- no special case in the gate, no new concept in drift detection.

DEPRECATION PLACEMENT, per the ruling: the 1.0.0 removal is recorded where a CONSUMER meets it -- the published `lore instructions` text and the release notes -- not only an ADR. Carried into LCLI-555 (published text), not done here.

LCLI-554 RE-SCOPE IS NOT YET EARNED. Under (c) the harness's three slug loops should pass unchanged, removing most of LCLI-554's atomicity. The orchestrator explicitly asked me to PROVE that rather than infer it, since the atomicity was well-founded under (a). LCLI-554 keeps its atomicity requirement until the harness is re-measured against a working alias, which cannot happen until this task lands.

IMPLEMENTED. Alias capability landed with slug ownership per ruling (c).

Shape: `aliases` joins TYPE_TABLE_KEYS and ParsedType (optional there, concrete on CompiledType, mirroring how `template` is handled so the built-in profile's seven type literals need no edit). parseTypes collects them; a new assertAliasesAreUnique runs AFTER the main loop, because an alias on the first [[types]] table can collide with a type declared further down and a single forward pass cannot see it. The compile loop seeds an alias into byLowerName AND bySlug — the same two maps as a canonical name, not a third map, so canonicalType and canonicalProfileType both learn aliases without either being edited and cannot drift apart over this. emitSchemaFiles emits one byte-identical file per alias spelling, which is what confers drift OWNERSHIP: schemaDriftFindings defines owned as whatever the emitter produces, so no special case was needed in the gate.

MUTATION TESTING FOUND TWO REAL DEFECTS IN MY OWN TESTS. Recording both, because the suite passing first time is exactly what the repo rule warns about.

1. A MUTANT DELETING THE ENTIRE byLowerName ALIAS SEEDING LEFT ALL 13 CASES GREEN. Cause: every alias fixture was SINGLE-WORD, and for a single-word alias the lowercased name and the lower-kebab slug are the same string ("Story" -> "story" both ways), so bySlug alone resolves it and the two seedings are indistinguishable. The suite asserted a property it did not test. Fixed by adding multi-word alias cases ("User Story" -> name "user story", slug "user-story"), which are the only fixtures that separate the two maps. A comment in the test file says so and says not to simplify them back.

2. THE DRIFT-OWNERSHIP TEST WAS SELF-SATISFYING. It built `committed` from emitSchemaFiles output and compared it against emitSchemaFiles output, so both sides moved together and it could only ever assert that the emitter agrees with itself — the exact shape schemaDriftFindings own docstring warns about one level up. It survived a mutant that deleted the alias emission outright. Fixed by building `committed` independently: the canonical-only export plus a story.schema.json, i.e. what a consumer repo actually holds across the rename.

FINAL MUTATION RESULTS, predictions read off the test file and all three matched exactly:
  M1 remove byLowerName alias seeding -> 1 red, the multi-word-by-exact-name case
  M2 remove bySlug alias seeding      -> 1 red, the multi-word-by-slug case
  M3 emitter drops alias files        -> 2 red, byte-identical emission + drift ownership
(M3 was predicted 2 and gave 1 BEFORE defect 2 was fixed; the corrected prediction is what is recorded here, and the miss is what exposed the circular test.)

VALIDATION: typecheck clean; bun test 3325 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail across 105 files; lore check 80 files 0 errors 0 warnings; biome reports 3 warnings and no errors, byte-matching clean origin/dev measured in a detached worktree so a pre-existing warning is not attributed here.

NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: no type is renamed, so this ships inert. The repo's own .lore/schemas is unchanged because no profile declares an alias yet — `[type.name, ...type.aliases]` reduces to `[type.name]`.

AC#5 WORDING CORRECTION, so the checkmark is not read as more than it is. The criterion says "npm run check exits 0". THERE IS NO `check` SCRIPT in this repo — package.json exposes lore, build, typecheck, format, lint, lint:shell, check:packages, lint:fix, test, test:browser, test:coverage. I wrote that criterion from the fleet SDLC guide’s generic phrasing without verifying it against this package.json.

What I actually ran, and what the checkmark stands for: `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm run lint` 3 warnings / 0 errors, byte-matching clean origin/dev measured in a detached worktree; `npm run format` (2 files, both mine); `npm test` 3325 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail across 105 files; `lore check` 80 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Recorded rather than silently substituted, because a criterion naming a command nobody can run is one a later reader cannot re-verify.
finalSummary: Alias capability with slug ownership, shipped inert. An alias seeds byLowerName and bySlug (the same two maps as a canonical name, so both mirror resolvers learn it unedited) and emitSchemaFiles writes a byte-identical file per alias spelling, which confers drift ownership without special-casing the gate. Mutation testing found two defects in the tests themselves -- a suite that stayed fully green with the byLowerName seeding deleted, because single-word aliases make name and slug the same string; and a self-satisfying drift test that compared the emitter against itself -- both fixed, with all three mutants now reddening predicted subsets exactly. Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#193, 14/14 checks green on head 5b6ce1c7, non-green 0.
